reconcile.note: Keil & Delitzsch trace the Elhanan-Goliath conflict to a copyist's slip in 2 Samuel 21:19, holding that the Chronicles reading naming Goliath's brother Lahmi is the original text.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats 2 Samuel 21:19 as the older text and reads Chronicles' added 'brother of' phrase as a later alteration shielding David's kill.

quotes.text: Elhanan the son of Jair of Bethlehem, we read in 2Samuel xxi. 19, was he who slew Goliath of Gath, the shaft of whose spear was as thick as a weaver's beam.… In Chronicles accordingly Elhanan smites the brother of the veritable Goliath.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel, trans. J. Sutherland Black & Allan Menzies (1885), on 2 Samuel 21:19 and 1 Chronicles 20:5.

sides.snippet: Then David ran, and stood over the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath of it, and killed him, and cut off his head therewith.
sides.verseText: Then David ran, and stood over the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath of it, and killed him, and cut off his head therewith. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

sides.snippet: Elhanan the son of Jaareoregim the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite's brother, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
sides.verseText: There was again war with the Philistines at Gob; and Elhanan the son of Jaareoregim the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite's brother, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
